# Skill: docs site HTML

## When to use

Use this skill when changing website pages, user-facing copy, layout structure, images, or light interactive behavior.

## Relevant files

- `*.html`
- `assets/css/*`
- `assets/js/*`
- `assets/images/*`
- `README.md`

## Expected practices

- Write for end users first.
- Keep content easy to scan on both mobile and desktop.
- Prefer semantic HTML and clear heading structure.
- Use CSS for presentation and JavaScript only for small enhancements.
- Keep calls to action clear, believable, and consistent across the site.
- Use meaningful alt text for informative images, and empty alt text for purely decorative images.

## Common pitfalls

- Using generic `div` elements where semantic elements are clearer
- Hiding important information deep in large text blocks
- Overusing JavaScript for behavior that HTML or CSS already handles well
- Leaving inconsistent business details across pages

## Verification

- Read the page as a customer would.
- Check whether the main action is obvious within a few seconds.
- Check that important details are easy to find and do not conflict with other content.
